value: peak frequency mean 91.27 kHz (SD 0.75, n = 28 bats)
structure: echolocation call (constant-frequency Rhinolophus call of a resting bat)
measurement: peak frequency, mean +/- SD, Table 3 row 'Peak frequency (kHz)', column 'R. osgoodi n = 28'; column order macrotis, osgoodi, ferrumequinum, affinis, pusillus
method: Materials and methods: 'The echolocation calls were recorded using an ultrasound recorder (UltraSound Gate 116, Avisoft Bioacoustics, Berlin, Germany) when the bats were resting in a temporary laboratory (5m x 4m x 3m), with the recording microphone aimed at the resting bat's head at a distance of 30cm' (joined from reader fragments, UltraSound Gate clause moved after 'recorder'). Analysed in Avisoft-SASLab Pro (1,024 FFT, 100% frame size, 93.75% overlap); peak frequency, Fmin and Fmax were the three call parameters; for each bat, after removing the first and last syllables of each call sequence, 15 syllables with a signal-to-noise ratio higher than 40 dB were randomly selected.
conditions: Wild bats mist-netted at the entrance of Xianren Cave (102.20E, 24.30N; Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, Yunnan, China) as they returned, August-September 2017 and 2018, 21:00 to 04:00; five rhinolophids coexist in the cave. Methods print '29 R. osgoodi (21 females and eight males)' captured; Table 3 header gives n = 28 for this species, so one captured bat is missing from the table and the paper does not say why. Recordings were of resting bats in a temporary laboratory, so the value is a resting-bat peak frequency, not a free-flight call; the paper does not say which harmonic was measured; the Table 3 caption says values are mean +/- SD, with Kruskal-Wallis or ANOVA across the five species (Chi-squared/F 53.59, p < 0.001 for the peak frequency row); no sex split of the call values is printed. Other species in the same table: R. macrotis 57.88 +/- 0.86 (n = 33), R. ferrumequinum 72.96 +/- 0.43 (n = 10), R. affinis 82.92 +/- 1.33 (n = 11), R. pusillus 101.92 +/- 1.49 kHz (n = 10).

method: Materials and methods 2.2: 'Echolocation calls were recorded using the PCTape system (480 kHz, 16 bit)' in a flight tent (5.0 m x 5.0 m x 3.5 m), after release of captured bats, and at roost emergence and near mist nets; the call parameters 'initial frequency (iF), terminal frequency (tF), bandwidth (BW) and pulse duration (PD)' were measured manually (Selena software, 256-point FFT, Hann window) and 'The beginning and the end of the signals were set at -30 dB below the maximal amplitude of the signal.' conditions: Wild bats captured at Ha Long Bay (Quang Ninh, 7-11 September 2020) and Ben Tre Province (Thanh Phu and Binh Dai districts, September 2019 to March 2021); Table 3 caption: 'Sound parameters of echolocating bat species from Ha Long Bay and Ben Tre Province.' n is the number of signals (not bats), measured from the first harmonic; the paper states no total of bats recorded for echolocation.
